dataset.title: Fibroblast specialisation across microanatomy in a single-cell atlas of healthy human Achilles tendon
dataset.authors: Cohen, C. J., Mimpen, J. Y., Snelling, S. J. B., et al.
dataset.journal: American Journal of Physiology - Cell Physiology
modalities: Spatial transcriptomics (10x Xenium custom probe panel)

cycle16_audit.cycle16_claim: The atlas contains 0 skeletal muscle myonuclei and excluded muscle tissue entirely.
cycle16_audit.evidence: Primary publication sampled the full muscle-tendon unit including the proximal myotendinous junction and adjoining muscle. Myonuclei and skeletal muscle parenchymal cells were captured and sequenced.

blocking_reasons.detail: Cohen et al. subclustered and annotated 6 fibroblast subtypes (mid-substance, paratenon, MTJ, muscle-specific, perineural, lining-layer). The published DEG tables (Data S1-S2) report fibroblast contrasts, not myonuclear contrasts.

Replicating the frozen Karlsen MTJCore signature requires a paired donor-level contrast between junctional myonuclei and mature non-junctional mid-belly myonuclei. Cohen et al. spatial and snRNA-seq tables do not provide this donor pseudobulk matrix.
Raw multi-gigabyte Seurat objects (Data S4-S5) are stored in external repository formats requiring extensive reprocessing to extract the minor myonuclear fraction.

stromal_mtj_characterization.biological_implication: Type XXII collagen is synthesized not only by myonuclei at myofiber ends, but also by specialized junctional fibroblasts in the tendon stroma. The MTJ attachment matrix is a co-product of myoblasts and fibroblasts.
